name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV traction inverters/onboard chargers, solar and wind inverters, motor drives) -- IndexBox (28 Sep 2026) projects 6-9% CAGR to 2035 with EV power electronics fastest at 10-14%, and India imports most of its capacitor film from China; Cosmo First already sells it and Jindal Poly Films' subsidiary JPFL Films announced a Rs 250 cr doubling, both small caps with thin media coverage, so still early (Cosmo First up ~31% in 6 months but down ~6% YoY; Jindal Poly +11% in 6 months), though capacitor film is a small share of both companies' revenue.
questions: What is capacitor-grade BOPP/PET dielectric film, how does it differ from packaging film (thickness 2.5-12 micron, metallisation, self-healing), and how big and fast-growing is the global market per IndexBox, Mordor, FMI and others?

What are the end-market demand drivers (EV traction inverters and onboard chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, industrial drives) and how is demand shifting toward thinner, higher-breakdown-voltage films?

How dependent is India on imported capacitor film (China, Japan, Korea), and what does the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) approval of metallised-film and passive-component projects mean for domestic film demand?

What exactly has Cosmo First done (Dec 2023 launch of metallised capacitor-grade BOPP, ~750 MT/yr, second metallizer, scale-up statements), and what are its current capacity, customers, qualification status and revenue contribution?

What has Jindal Poly Films / JPFL Films committed (Oct 2024 Rs 250 cr capacitor-film doubling, TDK testimonial, Rs 700 cr Nashik BOPP/PET/CPP capex): has the expansion been commissioned, what is the capacitor-film revenue, and how material is the SEBI show-cause notice of Aug 2026 as governance risk?

Do Polyplex, Uflex (Flex Films) or any other listed Indian film or capacitor maker have company-confirmed capacitor-grade capacity or plans (third-party reports name them, but confirm from filings before including)?
Which listed downstream Indian capacitor/passive-component makers or ECMS beneficiaries buy domestic film, and are there qualification or offtake tie-ups with film suppliers?
Has the market already priced this in: 6-12 month stock performance, valuation, and whether broker or mainstream media have run capacitor-film thematic pieces on these names?
What are the risks: polypropylene resin price volatility, Chinese overcapacity and pricing, slow customer qualification, small revenue share versus commodity packaging-film cycles, governance issues?

What are the catalysts: capacity commissioning, ECMS tranches, EV and solar inverter localisation, anti-dumping or import duty on capacitor film, customer approvals, quarterly disclosure of capacitor-film volumes?

film_producers_confirmed: Listed Indian companies with company-confirmed capacitor-grade film production or expansion
